Skellam Regression

Source: R/skellam.reg.R
skellam.reg.Rd

Fits a regression model assuming a Skellam distribution for the response variable.

Usage

skellam.reg(y, x)

Arguments

y

A vector of integers (positive or negative)

x

A matrix, vector or data.frame of covariates

Value

A list with components:

loglik

Maximized log-likelihood value

param1

Matrix for \(\lambda_1\) parameters:

  • Column 1: Estimated coefficients

  • Column 2: Standard errors

  • Column 3: Wald z statistics (coef/se)

  • Column 4: p-values (Wald test)

param2

Matrix for \(\lambda_2\) parameters (same structure as param1)

Details

The response is modelled as \(y_i = Y_{1i} - Y_{2i}\) with \(Y_{1i} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_{1i})\) and \(Y_{2i} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_{2i})\), so that param1 describes the rate of the counts that are added and param2 the rate of the counts that are subtracted, as in dskellam(y, lambda1, lambda2). Both rates use a log link, \(\log\lambda_{ki} = x_i^\top\beta_k\), with the same covariates (an intercept is added).

The log-likelihood is computed with dskellam(log = TRUE) and maximized by optim (BFGS) with the analytic gradient, starting deterministically from the moment estimates of an intercept-only model, so repeated calls give identical results. Standard errors come from the inverse of the observed information (optimHess). Observations with a missing response or covariate are removed with a warning. A warning is also given if the optimizer does not converge or the information matrix is not invertible (standard errors are then NA).

References

  • Skellam, J. G. (1946) The frequency distribution of the difference between two Poisson variates belonging to different populations. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A 109(3), 296.

  • Strackee, J.; van der Gon, J. J. D. (1962) The frequency distribution of the difference between two Poisson variates. Statistica Neerlandica 16(1), 17-23.

  • Karlis, D. and Ntzoufras, I. (2009) Bayesian modelling of football outcomes: using the Skellam's distribution for the goal difference. IMA Journal of Management Mathematics 20(2), 133-145.

Author

Michail Tsagris

Examples

set.seed(0)
x <- rnorm(100)
y1 <- rpois(100, exp(1 + 1 * x))
y2 <- rpois(100, exp(-1 + 1 * x))
y <- y1 - y2
skellam.reg(y, x)   # param1 near (1, 1), param2 near (-1, 1)
#> $loglik
#> [1] -195.8916
#> 
#> $param1
#>              Estimate Std. Error Wald value      p-value
#> (Intercept) 0.8944038 0.09865942   9.065569 1.239554e-19
#> x           0.9908116 0.06145987  16.121276 1.808368e-58
#> 
#> $param2
#>               Estimate Std. Error Wald value    p-value
#> (Intercept) -1.1752637  0.6720832 -1.7486879 0.08034498
#> x            0.1933462  0.7030906  0.2749947 0.78332035
#>
